sources.title: I used the AirPods 5 for nearly a week. They’re one of Apple’s best values ever
passages: The AirPods 5 are Apple's cheapest entry point into active noise cancellation yet, while also offering excellent sound quality and Live Translation.
The higher-end AirPods 5 add in on-ear volume controls, wireless charging and an extra hour of battery life.
Learn more The AirPods 5 just might be one of the best values that Apple’s ever offered.

For a starting price of $129, you get fantastic sound quality, a ton of features and some truly incredible active noise cancellation for a pair of breathable wireless earbuds that don’t burrow into your ears.
Factor in perks like live language translation and on-ear volume controls, and it’s somewhat shocking that these AirPods don’t have the word “Pro” in their name.

So, if you’re staring at that enticing $129 price tag and wondering if these should be your next AirPods, here’s what I think after nearly a week of wearing them while flying, commuting, working and even running in the pouring rain.
The AirPods 5 are Apple's cheapest entry point into active noise cancellation yet, while also offering excellent sound quality and Live Translation.
The higher-end AirPods 5 add in on-ear volume controls, wireless charging and an extra hour of battery life.

Even better, iOS 27 introduces a slider for Adaptive Audio in the Control Center that allows you to favor either noise cancellation or ambient awareness, giving you a fine level of control over your ANC experience that was previously exclusive to rival brands like Bose and Sony.
The AirPods 5’s sound quality is similarly superb for the price, highlighting my usual playlist of emo and pop tunes with plenty of oomph and detail.

The bouncy bass guitar of American Football’s “Blood on My Blood” came through with incredibly satisfying punch, all while giving the shiny synths, twinkly guitars and soft vocal croons plenty of space to shine on their own.
But I’d highly recommend that you try before you buy if possible, and certainly wouldn’t suggest using these as your main workout headphones for long-term vigorous activity.

While I love that the AirPods 5 have a cheaper starting price than before, I’m disappointed that Apple once again split its earbuds into two separate models that lock some key features behind a higher price.
Wireless charging has become a mainstay on wireless earbuds — I’ve seen it on models that cost less than $50 — so it’s a bummer that you have to pay $149 to have it on the AirPods 5.
You’ll also have to get the pricier model if you want the best possible battery life, which you’ll likely be tempted to do considering the base model’s four-hour ANC runtime.

I understand that concessions often have to be made to hit a lower price, but considering that the two AirPods 5 models only have a $20 price difference, I really wish Apple had found a way to consolidate all of these features into one affordable option.

It’s still somewhat shocking that you can get a $129 pair of Apple earbuds that offers immersive active noise cancellation, fantastic sound quality with Spatial Audio and even Live Translation for multiple languages.

The AirPods 5 are truly some of the best AirPods yet, getting you almost everything great about the AirPods Pro 3 for a significantly lower price (and in a more breathable open-style design that some folks might prefer).

Last generation, Apple offered two versions of the AirPods: one with active noise cancellation and one without .
They both also have adaptive audio and transparency mode, plus live translation with an iPhone 15 Pro or later, and are IP57 rated (up from IP54 on the AirPods 4).

The main differences between the $129 AirPods 5 and the $149 AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case — aside from the wireless charging case and the annoyingly long name — are the volume controls, battery life, and 20 bucks.

The biggest disappointment with the AirPods 5 is their battery life.
But the AirPods 4 redesign, which felt more comfortable in my ears, started to sway me.
Now with ANC at a cheaper price that includes volume control and a wireless charging case, the $149 AirPods 5 are great for someone who doesn’t like the feel of a sealed fit.
I wouldn’t even bother with the less expensive AirPods 5.
